topics.title: Track biology evals
topics.body:
Track biology evaluation coverage, tooling, and results for reference models and Snowball. This includes selecting benchmarks, defining comparable protocols, supporting their execution in Marin, and following results across models and checkpoints. The initial evaluation paths are non-agentic questions through Evalchemy and agentic biological analysis through Harbor.

[Biology evaluations catalog](https://openathena.ai/bio-evals/) · [Source repository](https://github.com/Open-Athena/bio-evals) — benchmark descriptions, task examples, implementation status, and linked issues/PRs.

Use Marin's existing protocols where available. Report question-answering and agentic-task results separately, with explicit task coverage and aggregation rules. Keep evaluation items isolated from training data.

The September 25 GLM-5.3 **Pi / BixBench-Verified-50** run on merged Harbor main completed with **39 correct / 46 graded (84.78%)**, **46/50 coverage (92%)**, and four ungraded outcomes. The [October 9 investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6086246928) identifies two output-truncation/non-submission cases, two agent timeouts followed by verifier timeouts, a Pi cancellation gap, and omission of verifier timeouts from the launch retry list. The exact cause of the verifier stalls remains unresolved. This run used 32,768 total context / 8,192 output tokens, Pi 0.87.0 with thinking enabled, and 30-minute agent / 5-minute verifier limits. No grades were changed or solver attempts rerun; verifier-only recovery lacked saved answers. Its protocol differs from the earlier Terminus-2 baseline below.

Current GLM-5.3 baselines (updated October 9, 2026):

| Benchmark / protocol | Correct / graded | Graded / attempted | Reported score | Agent solving time / question |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MMLU biology, Evalchemy | 462 / 554 | 554 / 554 (100%) | 81.79% mean of subject accuracies; 83.39% pooled accuracy | Not applicable (non-agentic) |
| [BixBench CLI v1.5, Harbor](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) | 101 / 187 | 187 / 205 (91.22%) | 54.01% among graded questions | Median **5.6 min**; middle 50% **1.7–15.5 min**; p90 **37.3 min**. 17/205 reached the 60-min cap. Excludes setup/grading. [Breakdown](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744679901) |
| [BixBench-Verified-50 v1.0 / Terminus-2 / decimal-precision-v1](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766684283) | 42 / 49 | 49 / 50 (98%) | 85.71% among graded questions; saved-answer regrade | Median **2.6 min**; p90 **15.7 min**; max **55.3 min**. Excludes setup/grading. [Breakdown](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766814742) |
| [BixBench-Verified-50 v1.0 / Pi 0.87.0 / decimal-precision-v1](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6086246928) | 39 / 46 | 46 / 50 (92%) | 84.78% among graded questions; four ungraded | 30-min agent cap; two tasks reached it. Median/p90 not computed. Excludes setup/grading. |

The BixBench run attempted all 205 questions and retains 18 ungraded outcomes: fourteen missing answers after the one-hour agent limit, two killed sandbox processes, one gateway failure, and one judge error. Marin's 95% interval accounting for ungraded items is 43.79–63.43%. Ten of eleven failed grading calls were recovered using saved answers; all 177 valid native grades and original artifacts were preserved, with no solver reruns.

BixBench uses Terminus-2 and Together `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, with the [explicit JSON-schema repair](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/97037f793efaae22e22da5b89bc9604d2e40e800), the unchanged binary-equivalence prompt, and disclosed 10 GiB disk / AMD64 image overrides. This is an exploratory CLI baseline. The replacement judge, answer-precision sensitivity, reference inconsistencies, missing grades, and unavailable exact serving weights revision limit comparisons. ID/OOD status remains unassigned. The [full result comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744365667) records revisions, budgets, recovery rules, and validation; EvalDash ingestion and panel visibility are verified.

The [answer review](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744559143) covers all 86 incorrect answers and all 18 ungraded outcomes. The subsequent [18-case adjudication](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744838386) records five confirmed task/reference defects, nine presentation-equivalence candidates (one with a method caveat), one submitted-answer precision error, and three unresolved reference/specification cases. Direct file checks confirm the gene-versus-record count, paired-tree aggregation, and mislabeled chromosome-length asset. A scalar/range screening pass includes all 205 outcomes and identifies cases that a blanket rounding rule would mishandle. Native grades remain unchanged; any revised task or scoring protocol must be versioned and reported separately. Fourteen other numerical/pipeline mismatches remain unresolved.

Relevant prior work: Harbor Index includes five BixBench-derived tasks. Its [merged instruction fixes](https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor-index/pull/142) specify previously unstated preprocessing/modeling choices for miRNA analysis (`bix-30-q1`) and ordinal regression (`bix-10-q2`), both present in this run. Its deterministic verifiers and 20-minute budgets differ from this baseline; its audits do not validate all BixBench reference calculations.

The standalone `bixbench-verified-50@1.0` port merged in [harbor#180](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180), closing [harbor#177](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/177). It preserves all 50 questions across 33 capsules from [Phylo revision c77fc8ea](https://huggingface.co/datasets/phylobio/BixBench-Verified-50/tree/c77fc8ea4611b546947b8a4710ed36ab72ee233c), credits Phylo's 17 question/answer revisions, and retains both known source defects (`bix-31-q2` and `bix-51-q8`). Existing BixBench variants and historical results are unchanged. The final [generated-task snapshot is 674c37ca8b2e](https://github.com/gonzalobenegas/harbor-datasets/tree/674c37ca8b2e537d36a1886f6cba99f2c6bdaa2f/datasets/bixbench-verified-50).

The September 21 Verified-50 run made one fresh GLM-5.3 attempt per question using Terminus-2, 32,768 input / 8,192 output tokens, default summarization, up to 16 concurrent trials, and 60-minute agent / 10-minute verifier limits. It used the disclosed 10 GiB disk override and pinned AMD64 image. The [native Harbor runtime was 17c0f88b](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/commit/17c0f88be98b357c0c27bbf7d7e5fd6e3e6b4e8a); the later merge commit was not the solver runtime. Exact served weights remain unavailable.

Original Verified-50 outcomes were 34 correct, 1 incorrect and 15 ungraded. The separate uniform regrade produced 42 correct, 7 incorrect and 1 ungraded, preserving all 35 original grades and the saved answers. It used the JSON-schema instruction and the explicit [decimal-precision-v1 policy](https://echo.oa.dev/wiki/496): 13 deterministic scalar comparisons and 36 Together GPT-OSS-120B calls, with no API errors, parsing errors or retries. GLM was not rerun. Original and intermediate results remain preserved; [archive and dashboard ingestion checks passed](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766684283). The curated subset and grading policy differ from the 205-question baseline, so their aggregate scores are not a controlled comparison.

The [Verified-50 seven-case audit](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766975987) found no adapter mapping or extraction defect, but identified a likely false negative for the 2.18-fold answer and unresolved reference conventions. These are not seven established model errors. The unanswered `bix-49-q4` failed with exit 143 after 55.3 minutes, before the agent limit; two R workers with 48 threads each were observed on two CPUs, but termination cause remains unconfirmed. [Harbor #192](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/192) tracks grading, reference ambiguities and this R failure together. No further grade changes or R rerun have been made.

### Follow-up: ungraded BixBench-Verified-50 Pi trials

Four of 50 trials remain ungraded: two reached the output limit without an answer file; two reached the agent timeout and subsequently timed out during verification. Missing retained artifacts prevent conclusive attribution to model behavior versus infrastructure. The [investigation](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6086246928) records the available evidence.

Before a future rerun, consider validating Daytona process cleanup and retaining submitted answers and partial verifier logs. These evaluation reliability improvements are deferred follow-up work; their role in the four missing grades remains unconfirmed. No rerun is currently planned.

Work to track:

- [ ] Select biology benchmarks and document the capabilities each measures, its limitations, and gaps in overall coverage. MMLU biology, BixBench CLI and BixBench-Verified-50 have initial baselines; additional non-agentic benchmarks remain to be selected, and ID/OOD assignments remain undetermined.
- [x] Establish the first Harbor-based biology evaluation, recording the benchmark variant, agent harness, and grading protocol. BixBench CLI baseline completed; result and limitations summarized above.
- [ ] Address integration gaps for selected benchmarks, including reusable configurations, launchers, scoring, and Eval Dash visibility.
- [x] Adopt the BixBench verifier JSON-schema instruction: [harbor#174](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/174) merged at `b78a0e52af98015fc8416d5bd5ee649a284e5a4c`, closing [harbor#166](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/166). The Verified-50 adapter bundles this revision; formatting repair does not establish numerical equivalence.
- [ ] Regenerate or explicitly patch existing BixBench registry tasks when adopting the JSON fix, with recorded task revisions. The template change does not alter historical snapshots.
- [x] Port Phylo's Verified-50 as a separate benchmark and complete its 50-question GLM-5.3 run, uniform saved-answer regrade and seven-case review. [harbor#180](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180) is merged; final results and protocol are recorded above.
- [ ] Resolve Verified-50 grading/reference ambiguities, the two retained source defects and the unanswered R task in [harbor#192](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/192). Preserve the 42-correct / 7-incorrect / 1-ungraded result; separately scope any policy change, source repair or diagnostic rerun. [Evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/180#issuecomment-5766975987).
- [x] Review all 86 incorrect answers and 18 ungraded outcomes in the full BixBench run; [findings and evidence](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744559143) distinguish observed analysis differences, reference/precision caveats and unscored failures.
- [x] Complete the evidence review of 11 precision/representation and 7 question/reference cases; [18-row decision table](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-5744838386), reproducible file checks, and seven local upstream-report drafts are available. No grades were changed.
- [ ] Review benchmark corrections in [harbor#167](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/issues/167), which contains all 18 cases, source revisions, reproduction details, and upstream decisions. Resolve the three remaining specifications (`bix-11-q5`, `bix-22-q6`, `bix-43-q4`) and define per-task numerical tolerances. Validate any revised scoring policy across all 205 outcomes, including existing passes, before reporting a separate result.
- [ ] Review Harbor Index's instruction fixes for `bix-30-q1` and `bix-10-q2` when specifying a corrected benchmark version; retain the original baseline protocol.
- [ ] Resolve the remaining 14 numerical/pipeline mismatches and document consequential reference preprocessing before selecting controlled reruns. Investigate missing-answer behavior and sandbox worker limits separately; exit-137 causes remain unconfirmed.
- [ ] Evaluate reference models and Snowball checkpoints under comparable protocols.
- [ ] Track results with model identity, task and evaluator revisions, per-task scores, coverage, failures, and aggregation rules so comparisons remain interpretable.
- [x] Complete the first GLM-5.3 MMLU biology evaluation and verify scores, full coverage, and Eval Dash ingestion.
- [x] Publish the initial biology-task configuration and runner on a branch, with code permalinks.

MMLU biology baseline (September 18, 2026):

GLM-5.3 was evaluated on three MMLU subjects on September 18, 2026. `MMLU-biology` names this selection: `mmlu_college_biology`, `mmlu_high_school_biology`, and `mmlu_medical_genetics`.

| Subject | Correct / questions | Accuracy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| College biology | 117 / 144 | 81.25% |
| High-school biology | 267 / 310 | 86.13% |
| Medical genetics | 78 / 100 | 78.00% |

All 554 questions were evaluated using Marin's five-shot answer-choice likelihood protocol, seed 42, and no item cap. The existing Eval Dash aggregate is **81.79%**, averaging the three subject accuracies equally. Accuracy across individual questions is **83.39% (462/554)**. No unanswered items or infrastructure errors were recorded; an audit of the native outputs reproduced every grade. [EvalDash run — Marina access required](https://marina.oa.dev/evaldash/runs/glm53-mmlu-biology-full-20260918-191647).

topics.title: [grug] Add the H100 pipeline foundation
topics.body:
Add a stage-local JAXPP pipeline for the full MoE model blocks, including latent/shared experts, SConv, attention positions and QB routing. Standard 1F1B remains the default. The synthetic runner supports the main recipe with FP32 parameters, BF16 compute and compute-scaled MuonH; the historical BF16 capacity recipe remains available.

Each routed expert parameter bank now shares one Frobenius norm across its experts, matching the stacked EP model. `--expert-normalization per_expert` provides an explicit comparison mode. `--qb-bias-mode frozen` retains the current pending QB bias while expert and router weights continue updating; adaptive QB remains the default. Numerical CPU regressions cover stacked-versus-stage-local updates and both QB state transitions.

The historical 48-layer, 65K synthetic diagnostic ran on 192 H100s with BF16-stored parameters and per-expert normalization. Its PP24/EP8/CP1 layout placed two layers in each stage and kept expert traffic within eight-GPU workers. It was chosen to establish capacity; no matched PP8/EP32/CP4 Megatron comparison was performed. The README records the later CP2 result and the differences in batch size and attention helpers. Historical hardware results do not validate the new normalization or frozen-QB option, and no SFT/RL quality comparison has been run.

The affected safe suite passed 2,391 tests with four skips and five expected failures. Focused CPU checks passed 86 tests with one skip; required lint, full type checking, strict docs and source links passed.

#9662 is stacked above this foundation and adds checkpoint/data support, the GB200 launcher, tracked runtime setup and bounded main-recipe hardware validation. Before merge, this foundation still owns replacing the positional result from `initialize_stage_local_pipeline_state`, centralizing the repeated backend/rematerialization identifiers, and separating the synthetic runner lifecycle in `pipeline_smoke.main`. These deferred changes require compiled-startup transport and optimizer-parking/warmup cleanup validation; #9662 then owns adapting its added checkpoint/data lifecycle.

topics.title: [RL] Add async Megatron launcher and score-centering study
topics.body:
Add a fully asynchronous Megatron/vLLM launcher for Snowball and Qwen, pinned to [MarinSkyRL #700](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/700). The launcher makes training, generation, evaluation, topology, context budget, checkpoint source, and artifact settings explicit. Score centering remains disabled by default.

The [study](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/goal/score-centering-launcher-01a0bb6f/experiments/post_training/score_centering_study.md) retains exact rendered configs, response-level scores, repeated evaluations, W&B histories, consumed-prompt trackers, Iris task costs, runtime failures, and quality curves against updates, loss tokens, elapsed time, and H100-hours. A matched-token A/B/C probe separates inference-versus-trainer engine mismatch from stale-weight drift. The signed terms partly cancel, so a stable aggregate magnitude does not show that stale-weight drift is negligible.

At the measured Qwen incumbent (TIS cap 1.05, top-k 32, token-weighted mean consumed age about 4.7 updates), the three exploratory seed pairs favored score centering by +36.5, +43.5, and +9 answers out of 756. Three prespecified confirmation pairs gave +28.5, -23.5, and -5.5. The confirmation mean is -0.2 answers with a paired 95% Student-t interval of -65.8 to +65.4; the six-seed descriptive mean is +14.8 (-12.6 to +42.1). The initial signal did not replicate consistently. Matched exposure, loss tokens, elapsed time, and cost show no compute saving at this setting. Because no acceptable quality-loss margin was selected, the result does not establish non-inferiority.

The format-fixed Snowball pair completed nine updates per arm with active TIS and finite score centering. Six evaluations of the same step-five weights varied more than the small arm difference: completed-answer endpoint differences ranged from -33 to +11 out of 756, while baseline-adjusted differences ranged from -20 to +24. The original 4,096-token run completed updates six through nine, then failed during update ten. Five matched continuations restored the arm-specific step-five checkpoints with response caps from 3,840 down to 1,536 tokens, but each failed before completing resumed update six in TransformerEngine's unfused attention path. The configs requested FlashAttention; retained runtime logs show that installed FlashAttention 2.8.4 was outside the supported range through 2.8.3, so the runtime fell back to unfused attention. This report therefore makes no Snowball quality claim past step five.

Round-two diagnostics, Qwen confirmation, Snowball qualification, retries, generation, evaluation, and discarded work consumed 1,072.548303 reserved H100 task-hours. The measured evidence supports keeping score centering off by default in the tested Qwen range. Further Snowball training requires a runtime or backend change, or a severe response-length reduction that would materially change the experiment. A compatible FlashAttention attempt must first verify that the fused backend is active.

The final High-tier goal review found no implementation correctness defect. Its two completion blockers, omitted diagnostic task costs and missing clean-pair YAMLs, are fixed in `928887f72d`. Targeted launcher and cost tests pass. CI is running on that final review-fix commit.

topics.title: Close hero data loaders before JAX shutdown
topics.body:
Stop the hero training data loader and join its prefetch thread after successful training, before JAX shutdown. A live prefetch thread caused shutdown crashes between benchmark arms. Keep the progress watchdog active during the join and skip the join after a training or final-checkpoint exception.

Finalize unbuffered loaders’ async generators on their producer event loop before stopping it, so JAX mesh-context cleanup runs on the correct thread.

Extracted from #9228. These lifecycle fixes are independent of attention backend selection. Tests cover producer termination and generator finalization on the producing thread.

Affected safe tests: 1,216 passed, 13 skipped. Lint and type checks pass.

topics.title: Clear masked shared-memory tiles in segmented FA4 backward
topics.body:
Clear masked shared-memory entries before the existing segmented FA4 backward kernel copies queries, keys, values, and output gradients. Its synchronous copies leave masked destinations unchanged, but matrix operations still read those entries. Stale NaNs can therefore propagate through products with zero.

Add a GB200 test that repeatedly compares partial-tile outputs and gradients against the float32 reference.

Extracted from #9228. This fixes the existing segmented kernel independently of native SM100 kernel selection.

The [GB200 regression](https://iris.oa.dev/#/job/%2Fmwittmann%2Ffa4-scope-port-20260922b) passes. The run used CPU Torch 2.11.0 to avoid main’s unrelated `libcufile.so.0` import failure. Seven affected safe tests pass locally; lint and type checks pass.

topics.title: Add correctness-gated GDN-2 TPU kernels
topics.body:
Add experimental single-device Gated DeltaNet-2 kernels and a correctness-gated benchmark. Vendor only Atomic Ops' four compute files at a9bd7c5315907d23ccf1ce6b033d46a196566888 as the baseline, retaining the MIT license and original arithmetic. The modified candidate replaces off-diagonal pairwise exponentiation and reduction with matrix products, and masks noncausal pairs before exponentiation. It has no clipping, non-finite replacement, or solve damping.

Repeated matched sweeps show 3.05–3.27x faster forward+backward on v5e/v5p and 3.12–3.22x on v6e than each device's fastest tested baseline configuration, for batches 4/8, 4096 tokens, and six 128-dimensional heads in FP32/BF16. The v6e forward-only speedup is 5.36–5.62x. Outputs, final state, and gradients for q/k/v/w/b/g and the initial state pass an independent CPU recurrence before either timing mode is accepted. All four TPU generations select 128-token chunks; the solve microblock is 16 tokens on v4/v5e/v5p and 32 on v6e. Batches 5–7 are unmeasured interpolation.

The v4 candidate passes the same representative shapes; all four hardware types pass separate batch-1, 512-token stress tests with log-decays sampled down to -5. The baseline does not compile on v4; no baseline speedup is claimed there. The v4 256-token configuration exceeds VMEM. Its selected 128-token, batch-8 FP32 forward-only measurements include periodic outliers. v6e's selected tile repeats within 0.22%, but other tile configurations also show outliers. All timing samples are retained.

[Measurement artifacts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3df6efef5a0fb18928e72673e9fd5f769749ae15/docs/reports/data/gdn2-tpu-20260922/README.md) retain exact source snapshots, hardware settings, compilation costs, and caveats. The [kernel reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3df6efef5a0fb18928e72673e9fd5f769749ae15/docs/references/gdn2-kernels.md) documents reproduction and explicit tuning fallback. Affected unit tests, lint/type checks, and documentation-link checks pass. Model integration and training are outside this change.

topics.title: [vllm histograms] Store and query cumulative family snapshots
topics.body:
Store cumulative histograms as one record per engine and family and query them alongside scalar history. Disjoint integer bucket counts and floating-point bounds use existing `kind=histogram` records and the nullable `body_json` column. Scalar histogram observations and the scalar snapshot publisher retain their behavior. No new record kind, table, column, data backfill, or schema migration is needed.

The detailed and compact dashboard queries share histogram component normalization, publication validation, and delta calculation. A scalar publication supplies a baseline only when count, sum, and all bucket bounds known at that publication are present. Scalar counts at or above 2^53 are unavailable because their floating-point representation cannot guarantee exact source integers. Both queries reject conflicting copies and negative interval-bin counts. Identified scalar publications use their final component timestamp for query-window selection; untagged scalar publications must fit wholly within the window. The compact summary reads bucket rows for legacy scalar histograms and per-bin arrays for structured histograms. Epoch and sequence must either both be supplied or both be absent; an absent pair uses collection time as publication identity. The three-minute lookback retains duplicate copies for validation before selecting baselines. Structured buckets use one cumulative prefix sum. Equivalent numeric bucket spellings share a canonical label; integral labels render without `.0`. The dashboard withholds percentile and distribution estimates when a family has multiple bucket-bound schemas, including across scalar and structured publications. Client bounds are validated as 64-bit floating-point numbers, matching the server. Structured counts from 0 through 2^63-1 are supported; larger source counts are reported as publication loss.

In September 23–24, 2026 local measurements, a 32-engine, eight-family publication persisted 832 structured versus 6,208 scalar vLLM data rows and used 2 versus 8 HTTP POSTs. Row counts include histograms, gauges, and counters. A four-engine, three-hour replay reduced ingest time from 180.17 to 33.50 seconds. Its 30-minute detailed query preserved time-to-first-token mean and p50/p90/p99, with higher structured client peak RSS (474 versus 441 MB). A separate 32-engine, two-minute replay preserved output-length and time-per-output-token means, counts, and percentiles, plus all output-length bins. These historical single-job measurements do not establish current-head performance or the seven-day, 50-job overview query's 10-second target. The vLLM overview rejects results with more than one million input samples.

The root development lock uses DuckDB 1.5.4, matching the Grafana package lock for the new bucket expansion. Regional Finelog schemas, external histogram SQL consumers, and the released Rigging publisher in MarinSkyRL's frozen environment require verification before rollout. Part of #9382.

topics.title: [grug] Add the Hero-mix and quality-classifier fast tracks
topics.body:
* add two data fast tracks next to the model ladder. all three tracks train the same dense/MoE ladder (d512–d1280) on 8×H100 and compare on final Paloma macro loss
* model ladder: `fast-track` trains on the frozen `hero_tok/v16384_shuf/train` cache, as before
  * `launch.py` resolves the budget in `resolve_h100_ladder_budget` and takes a `TrainingSource`, so the data tracks use the same training wiring
  * add `--seed` and `--data-seed`. `--submit` forwards `WANDB_MODE` and accepts `WANDB_MODE=disabled` without `WANDB_API_KEY`
* hero mix plus a new dataset: sample the production Hero mixture and give a new Hugging Face dataset a fraction `p` of the training tokens
  * `hero_sample_cli` replays `harrier_mix_2026_08_18.json` over `store_4d2e363d` in the production loader order and retokenizes each source segment as BOS + text + EOS with `hero-bpe-v16384` into a `PreparedHeroSample`. build it once at the largest ladder budget (17,478,713,344 tokens) and use it again for all rungs
  * `add_dataset_cli` tokenizes a bounded HF prefix at an immutable revision, scales the Hero weights by `1 - p`, and caps the new data at `C = min(p·B, (N/T)·B)` to simulate the production epoch count [^1]
  * `hero_baseline_cli` trains the matched control on the same `PreparedHeroSample`
  * the Hero cell capacity check runs on the final mixture weights, so a small `p` cannot make the largest cell repeat its data
* quality classifier: sample raw text from all 292 registered sources in proportion to corpus size, score it with a frozen head, and train on the top documents
  * `corpus_sample_cli` builds a `RawCorpusPool` with `corpus-id-interval-v1`: one seeded cyclic interval in the 128-bit document-ID space for each source. it skips a row group only when its ID statistics show no overlap. `--label-exclusion-manifest` is required
  * `quality_labels_cli` freezes the GLM-5.2 labels and fits a ridge head on cached Harrier features (target `(quality - 1) / 4`, 80/10/10 split by duplicate group). the raw pool excludes all labelled duplicate groups
  * `quality_cli --stage features|score|select|train` scores the pool once at the largest rung. for budget `B`, it ranks the first `10·B` raw tokens and keeps whole documents until they fill `B`. `--selection-method candidate|incumbent|random` gives the matched controls
* the data-track CLIs default to MoE and derive `--data-seed` from `--seed`, the same as `fast-track`
* add `fast-track-long-string-v1` for HF and raw-corpus tokenization: split at the first whitespace at or after 10,000 characters, and reject a document above 64 MiB with its source and ID
  * bound native tokenizer batches by bytes. a local 32 MiB probe kept all 19,532,169 token IDs, and peak RSS went from 4.60 GiB to 2.85 GiB
* rename `max_train_batches` → `max_train_sequences` in `LmDataConfig`, so a component cap does not depend on the batch size
* fixes found during the runs
  * iris: repair missing CUDA toolchain files. put the child job and attempt in JAX coordinator names, because sibling training jobs connected to the coordinator of a different job
  * fray: pass actor concurrency to Iris RPC servers, because the 32-thread default let long waits block worker heartbeats. the inference broker sets its concurrency explicitly
  * datakit CPU drivers install the `cpu` group with `datakit`, so that they do not resolve the CUDA Torch wheel
  * artifact loading keeps absolute bucket paths, grug dispatch forwards `WANDB_MODE`, and levanter keeps eval metrics between detail intervals
* results at this time (seed 0, final macro loss from the training logs [^2])
  * hero mix, MoE, change against the Hero baseline at the same rung [^3]:

    | rung | 10% Paloma | 10% Uncheatable | 99% Paloma | 99% Uncheatable |
    |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
    | d512 | +4.22% | +1.95% | +58.70% | +68.40% |
    | d768 | +3.30% | +1.56% | +56.97% | +63.72% |
    | d1024 | +4.28% | +1.51% | +55.47% | +61.68% |
    | d1280 | not valid | not valid | +48.85% | +60.26% |

  * each valid mixed run is worse on all 23 evaluation datasets. for 10% at d512 dense, three matched seeds changed Paloma loss by +0.05%, +0.05%, and −0.14%
  * quality, four-source pilot (`cp/arxiv_abstracts`, `cp/wikiteam`, `docx-corpus/en`, `starcoder2/documentation`, 6,064,023 documents): ridge selection against random selection gave Paloma macro BPB 1.9051 against 1.6164, and 20 of 23 datasets were worse
  * these probes test the mechanics. they use assumed production counts and one seed, so they do not show the value of WikiText or of the ridge head
* open work
  * build the `resample-v2` Hero sample and run the four-scale Hero-mix comparison again on it
  * the all-292 raw pool stopped after about 14 h: `stack-v3` has documents of 79–213 MB, above the 64 MiB limit. a policy is necessary (drop and count, raise the limit, or exclude the source). no four-scale quality run exists yet
  * the 10% d1280 run resumed from a temporary checkpoint after a preemption near step 14.1k. its training loss went from 1.45 to 2.75 and did not recover, so the result is not valid. the cause is not known
  * training reads the new dataset in HF prefix order, because the Hero mixture uses `shuffle=False` and Levanter has no shuffle for one component
  * the pool excludes only the candidate's labels, not the training labels of an incumbent scorer
* remove the DataKit end-to-end track from this PR [^4]

[^1]: `N` is the number of available unique tokens in the new dataset, `T` is the production budget (default 18.75T), and `B` is the rung budget. the loader cap rounds down to whole sequences.
[^2]: these runs used W&B offline mode, so the values come from the `levanter.eval` log lines.
[^3]: these runs used the earlier resampler, which kept the source BOS as text and did not put an EOS after the last segment of a source example. the control and the treatment used the same sample, so each delta compares like with like, but the sample differs from `resample-v2`. old `PreparedHeroSample` and `PreparedAddDatasetCache` artifacts must be prepared again.
[^4]: this removes `--source-mode sample|registry`, the token-shuffle control, the shared Zephyr pool (`execution_scope`), and coordinator driver placement in the reference DataKit pipeline. the 25B-sample results and controls are in an earlier revision of this description.

topics.title: [fast-track] Marin Belay v1: hill-climb the scaling ladder (Paloma macro loss, 8 min on 8×H100)
topics.body:
This issue tracks iterative improvements to the Marin pretraining scaling ladder (`experiments/grug/fast_track`) using the **Marin Belay** process. It is a twist on autoresearch: an agent runs experiments in batches, and anyone can steer it with research directions. > **To suggest a research direction, comment on [Marin Belay Intake (#9514)](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9514).** Suggestions a maintainer approves (👍 from a `marin-devs` member) are copied into this thread automatically, and the agent acts only on this thread. This thread holds the agent's batch reports and maintainer steering. ![fast_track MoE ladder: Marin 535B baseline, clean KMA and candidate 9](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/marin-community/marin/9697c11ef215ec0f9d536a1bceb0876f768fcf26/v1/ladder_scaling.png) The Marin 535B compute-optimal baseline follows `L(C) = 1.2 + 59.0·C^(−0.0843)` over four data-matched rungs. Clean KMA, the current baseline (★), is 0.022 lower at d512, 0.049 lower at d768, 0.040 lower at d1024 and 0.033 lower at d1280, which is about 1.14×, 1.43×, 1.40× and 1.35× the baseline's compute efficiency. Its dashed curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 64.8·C^(−0.0870)`. The **?** marks the open question this issue is chasing: how much further down each point can go. The red diamonds are the current best recipe, candidate 9 (Status below): **2.977 / 2.725 / 2.515 / 2.397** at d512 / d768 / d1024 / d1280. d512 and d768 are seed means, and the bigram table follows rule A. d768–d1280 are data-matched; d512 sits at its fixed-time step count (2817 vs 2383 steps), so it's plotted slightly to the right. That is 0.157 / 0.098 / 0.078 / 0.074 below clean KMA. Its dash-dot curve is fit to all four points: `L(C) = 1.2 + 55.0·C^(−0.0847)`. Its slope is a little shallower than clean KMA's, so the gap narrows with compute: projected to **1e24 FLOPs, 1.710 vs clean KMA's 1.727, about 1.48× clean KMA's compute efficiency and 2.95× the 535B baseline's**. Because the fixed-time d512 point flattens the fitted slope, that projection is probably conservative. The right panel is clean KMA's training MFU at each rung on one 8×H100 node: 9.5% at d512 and d768, 12.2% at d1024, and 13.0% at d1280. FLOPs are counted from KMA's own layers (KDA, MLA + Inkling, AttnRes), as 3× forward with no recompute. The trainer's logged `throughput/mfu` uses the baseline architecture's FLOP formula, so it is slightly off for KMA. ## Objective **Minimize Paloma macro loss (`eval/paloma/macro_loss`, final step) at the d512 rung after a fixed 8 minutes of 8×H100 train-step time.** - **Fixed time, not fixed tokens.** Faster code trains on more tokens within the 8 minutes, so a pure speedup counts as a win. - The LR schedule depends on the step count, so fix steps before each run: `num_steps = round(480 s × ex/s ÷ batch)`. - Measure ex/s with a short `--no-eval` probe (~30 steps) on the same cluster, and use the steady-state throughput. - Compile, evals and startup are excluded from the 8 minutes. - **Numerics changes are allowed** (e.g. FP8, precision changes, approximate kernels). They count as ordinary wins; no parity check needed. - **Noise.** Differences under ~0.005 are noise. A win must beat the current best by more than 0.005. ### Gates (both relative to the current baseline, same fixed-time rule at each rung) - **Gate 1:** beat the baseline at d512 and d768. - **Gate 2:** also beat it at d1024 and d1280, **and** project to lower Paloma macro loss at 1e24 FLOPs. Fit a power law of final loss against training FLOPs across the four rungs, for both the baseline and the variant, fixing the asymptote to 1.2. ### Fixed - Training data, the 16k BPE tokenizer, and the eval sets. - Sequence length 4096. - One 8×H100 node per rung. - The FLOP accounting used for the gate-2 projection. ### Judgment calls - **Hero-scale speed is out of scope for v1, so use discretion.** - Robust target criteria would also check training speed and inference speed at hero scale. Marin Belay v1 skips those checks. - Judge whether a change's d512 gain would carry over to hero scale, and avoid changes whose gain comes from d512-only effects. Two examples: - Dropping MoE for dense would be a clear win at d512 because dense gets ~5× higher MFU there, but that MFU gain would not carry over at hero scale. - A much larger KV cache would also be a clear win at d512, but it would hurt long-context inference speed. - **Avoid magic numbers.** - Prefer changes with few new tuned constants. A tuned constant is justified when its gain is above the noise threshold and holds as a pattern across scales. For example, a 2× LR on one parameter group qualifies if it clears the noise threshold and the gain shows up consistently at larger rungs. - The higher a change's risk of curve fitting, the more scales it must be validated at before it counts as a win. - **Spend effort in proportion to an idea's likelihood of improvement.** - Promising ideas deserve several attempts. Long shots can be tried once and dropped. - A first run is not a verdict for a large change. If you try a new architecture or component, tune its optimizer assignment, LR, init and other key hyperparameters before concluding it doesn't work. The baseline's settings were tuned for the baseline, not for the new idea. ## Architecture (current best, d512) The diagrams below show **clean KMA**. Build from this branch. The recipe below covers every model and optimizer component. Values are for d512 unless noted; the code is `experiments/grug/fast_track/{model,optimizer,heuristic,launch}.py`. **Shape** | Rung | Width D | Layers | Local (KDA) / global (MLA) layers | Heads × head dim | Batch | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | d512 | 512 | 6 | 4 / 2 | 4 × 128 | 128 | | d768 | 768 | 8 | 6 / 2 | 6 × 128 | 128 | | d1024 | 1024 | 12 | 9 / 3 | 8 × 128 | 256 | | d1280 | 1280 | 14 | 10 / 4 | 10 × 128 | 256 | - Every 4th layer and the last layer are global; all other layers are local. - The run uses a 16k vocab and sequence length 4096 with packed documents. Every ShortConv and the KDA state respect document boundaries (the KDA state resets at each document start). - Weights are initialized with std 0.5/√D. Compute is bf16. **Embedding and output** - Token embedding → RMSNorm → GatedNorm. The result is AttnRes source 0. - Output path: final AttnRes gate → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → untied lm_head (`output_proj`). - The fused lm_head + cross-entropy loop uses a vocab tile of 8192. - GatedNorm (every GatedNorm in the model) is `x · sigmoid(W_up · SiLU(W_down · x))`, with a rank-128 bottleneck. **Block (every layer)** - **Attention sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → mixer (KDA or MLA). - **MoE sublayer:** input = its AttnRes gate mix → RMSNorm → GatedNorm → MoE → ShortConv on the MoE output. - Each ShortConv is a 4-tap causal depthwise conv. **Local layers: Kimi Delta Attention** (Kimi K3's layer) - **Projections:** q/k/v are D → N·128 with full heads (no GQA). Each goes through a ShortConv followed by SiLU. q and k are L2-normalized, and q is scaled by 1/√128. - **Decay:** per-channel log-decay `g = −5·sigmoid(exp(A_log)·(x·W_a_down·W_a_up + dt_bias))`. - The gate projection has rank 128. - `A_log` is one value per head, initialized to 0. - `dt_bias` is one value per channel, initialized so the decay rate spans 0.02–0.5. - **Write strength:** `β = sigmoid(x·W_β)`, one value per head. - **Recurrence:** `S_t = (I − β·k·kᵀ)·Diag(exp(g))·S_{t−1} + β·k·vᵀ`, read out as `o_t = S_tᵀ·q_t`. - It runs as chunked Pallas kernels, with a stable block-doubling inverse inside each chunk. - **Output:** per-head RMSNorm with a learnable 128-wide scale shared across heads → full-rank per-channel gate `sigmoid(x·W_g)` → `W_o`. - No positional encoding, no window, no XSA, and no ShortConv on the branch output. **Global layers: MLA + Inkling relative position** - **q:** full-rank, D → N·128 (no Q latent). - **k and v:** k = `W_uk · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)` and v = `W_uv · RMSNorm(x·W_dkv)`. - They share one 512-wide KV latent, with a learnable RMSNorm on the latent. - Heads are 128 wide with no RoPE part. - There's no ShortConv on K, so the up-projections can be absorbed at inference. - **Scaling:** no QK-norm; `qk_mult` = 1, i.e. standard 1/√128 logit scaling. - **Position — Inkling relative-position bias**, added to the pre-softmax logits in place of RoPE: - `bias[h,i,j] = R[i,h,:] · P[:, i−j]`, where `R = x·W_r` is 16 values per head. - `P` is a bank of shape [16 × 1024] shared across heads. The relative extent is 1024. - It runs inside the FA4 attention kernel (forward, backward, and the SM90 backward pass). - **XSA** (exclusive self-attention): subtract the component of each head's output that is parallel to its own value vector. - **Output gate:** per head, `2·sigmoid(x·W_gate)`. `W_gate` is zero-initialized, so the gate is 1 at init. - The branch output also gets a ShortConv. **MoE sublayer (LatentMoE with quantile-balanced routing)** - **Experts:** 384 routed experts, top-8. Each is a SwiGLU with hidden size D/2. - **Latent space:** experts operate in a D/2-wide latent. The input goes through `W_latent_down` → RMSNorm, and the combined expert output goes back up through `W_latent_up`. - **Router:** reads the full-width token and computes logits in fp32. - Experts are selected by top-(8+1) on bias-adjusted logits, where the 9th logit is the threshold α. - Combine weights are the sigmoid of the unbiased logits, renormalized to sum to 2.5. - **Quantile balancing:** each step, each expert's threshold β is the global (1 − K/E) quantile of the logit margins (logit − α), read from a 10k-bin histogram. The router bias is set to −β. - The router bias is not trained by gradient. - **Capacity:** capacity factor 1.15, with pooled-wave expert-parallel dispatch. Receiver ranks are sort-based and the expand backward is gather-based. - **Shared experts:** 2 shared SwiGLU experts that bypass the latent: D → D/2 hidden → D. - **Fused projections:** - The router, latent-down, and both shared experts' gate/up projections run as one GEMM. - The shared experts' down-projections run as one GEMM. **Residual stream: Block Attention Residuals** - **Sources:** the embedding source, one running sum per completed block of sublayer outputs, and the running partial sum of the current block. - The model has 8 blocks. Block sums use the raw sublayer outputs. - **Gates:** every sublayer (attention and MoE) has its own gate, and there is one final gate before the output norm. Each gate has one learned pseudo-query `q ∈ ℝᴰ`, zero-initialized so every gate starts as a uniform average. - **Mixing:** per token, `logitᵢ = q · rms_norm(sourceᵢ)`, using a parameter-free (frozen) RMS key norm, then `softmax` over sources and a weighted sum of the raw sources. - **Implementation:** - Each completed block is scored once against every gate that reads it. - Backward: at d512 the layer's forward intermediates are saved. At d768–d1280 each layer is recomputed. At d1280 the attention branch is also rematerialized. - The model keeps one layer stack per mixer kind. **Optimizer** | Group | Update rule | LR | Parameters | |---|---|---|---| | `muonh` | MuonH | MuonH LR | all attention and MoE matrices: MLA `W_q`/`W_dkv`/`W_uk`/`W_uv`/`W_o`; KDA `W_q`/`W_k`/`W_v`/`W_o`/`W_g`; experts; shared experts; latent down/up. Also every GatedNorm `W_down`/`W_up`. | | `kda_beta` | MuonH | 2 × MuonH LR | KDA `W_β` | | `adamh` | AdamH | MuonH LR | lm_head (`output_proj`) | | `adam` | Adam | Adam LR | token embedding; router; attention output gate; router bias slot (overwritten by QB); all 1-D norm gains; ShortConv kernels; KDA `W_a_down`/`W_a_up`, `A_log`, `dt_bias`; Inkling `W_r` and `P` | | `attn_res_query` | Adam | 0.1 × Adam LR | the AttnRes pseudo-queries | - **MuonH:** Nesterov momentum 0.95 → Newton–Schulz orthogonalization (5 quintic steps, bucketed across same-shape matrices) → a step along that direction, then projection back onto the matrix's Frobenius sphere. Each matrix's norm stays fixed at its init value. - **AdamH:** the Adam direction with the same Frobenius-sphere (hyperball) projection. - **Adam:** β1 0.9. Only the router and the attention output gate get decoupled weight decay (0.02). No other parameter gets weight decay, and there's no gradient clipping. - **Schedule:** 1% warmup, then linear decay to 0.05× peak. - **Peak values** from `MoeHeuristic` (they depend on tokens, width and batch): - Adam LR = `0.0876 · tokens^−0.346 · D^−0.345 · √(tokens per batch)`. - MuonH LR = 13/3 × Adam LR. - β2 = `0.999^(tokens per batch / 131072)`. - ε = `9.68e−18 · √(steps)`. - At d512 with 2384 steps: MuonH LR 0.0227, Adam LR 0.0052, β2 0.996, ε 4.7e−16. topics.title: [eval] Code task records lose graded coverage
topics.body:
A successful Evalchemy run for HumanEval+, MBPP+, and CRUXEval writes valid task metrics but records every attempted sample as ungraded. Downstream statistics read zero coverage and cannot form uncertainty intervals from the run.

The Snowball parent run wrote:

- HumanEval+: `pass_at_1=0.5182926829`, `n_attempted=164`, `n_scored=0`, `ungraded=164`
- MBPP+: `pass_at_1=0.4206349206`, `n_attempted=378`, `n_scored=0`, `ungraded=378`
- CRUXEval: `input_pass@1=0.04625`, `output_pass@1=0.08875`, `n_attempted=1600`, `n_scored=0`, `ungraded=1600`

Reproduce:
1. Run Evalchemy tasks `HumanEvalPlus`, `MBPPPlus`, and `CruxEval` with native FineStore output.
2. Read `metrics` and `coverage` from the completed record.
3. Observe valid aggregate scores with all samples marked ungraded.

Run: `/rav/snowball-python-expert-baseline-1-coord`

Record: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/20260929-024736-snowball-python-expert-parent-coding-expert-code-93c7/record.json`

Expected: a successful aggregate score records its exact graded count. HumanEval+ and MBPP+ emit `scored_count`, but `task_item_count()` does not recognize that key. CRUXEval emits pass rates without an aggregate count, so its adapter must also publish the number of graded examples. Partial or contradictory runs must remain ungraded.

Issue #9528 will use the canonical aggregate metrics for the parent comparison and will state that this record cannot support sample-level uncertainty.

topics.title: [eval] Check in the September evaluation campaign
topics.body:
Check in the model, evaluator, and launcher configurations for the September 2026 evaluation campaign, together with the runtime fixes needed for serving, retry, resume, and coverage. The launcher validates external pins, writes immutable effective-config snapshots, and accepts an optional submitter-controlled version label. That label does not attest policy conformance.

Harbor results are bound to the full model and hosted judge configurations, dataset, policy, runtime, and task limit. Resume checks this identity before submission and reuse. A changed checkpoint under the same served name is rejected, as are existing roots without model-bound provenance. Recovery retries known infrastructure failures and unscored trials while retaining scored outcomes and unknown errors.

The frozen Harbor runtime pins 94b118022fe3e677784a638daf33d57a836fa5fe and includes the Tau3 adapter. The Evalchemy lock and generated pin match Marin's external dependency configuration.

SWE-bench uses the native Mini-SWE adapter from merged [Harbor #232](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/232) and [#233](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/233). Its 32,768-token context includes the prompt and reply together. Mini-SWE counts the rendered prompt through the serving tokenizer, including tools and the generation prefix, and caps the reply within the remaining budget and server window. Harbor loads Mini-SWE's base configuration before applying overrides and selects its batch agent, which saves the trajectory on context exhaustion without prompting. Harbor can then verify the existing patch.

Sotopia uses the packaged agent from merged [Harbor #231](https://github.com/marin-community/harbor/pull/231). Judge failures become verifier infrastructure errors. The Marin agent wrappers and their harness dependencies are removed. Sotopia's native generation still does not enforce its declared context budget, so those results cannot establish conformance to the 32K context policy.

Part of #9566.

topics.title: [RL] Run async and Snowball launchers on Megatron with rollout buffers
topics.body:
Run async Snowball training with Megatron and the standard rolling rollout buffer. Every async preset uses `behavior_clip`, including the staleness-zero on-policy preset; the default and on-policy presets have identical training settings except for staleness. Rollouts use the tokenizer's built-in chat template to preserve sampled completion token IDs and behavior log probabilities. The policy loss uses `off_policy_correction: none`. Megatron AdamW applies weight decay to every trainable parameter in Snowball async training. The final training checkpoint queues an HF conversion request for the launcher's HF exporter when training finishes. Async runs accept `--target-cluster` with `cw-us-east-02a` or `cw-rno2a`; the policy's east cluster remains the default, and training and evaluation use the selected cluster.

Curriculum policies default to Megatron and carry model-specific parallelism in their policy specifications. Snowball curriculum reserves two nodes for reference models, uses activation checkpointing and offloads optimizer state during rollouts. Its R4/R5 presets select MuonH with four policy pipeline stages and one sequence per microbatch. Microbatch size changes memory use and speed only; token-mean loss is normalized over the whole optimizer step. These presets need a MarinSkyRL revision with the Megatron MuonH optimizer (marin-community/MarinSkyRL#820). The shared runtime selects the pinned Megatron dependency profile for Iceball, TaskTrove, CatCount and online-EAGLE as well.

The launcher configurations compose against Marin's pinned MarinSkyRL revision `27c0bc8a`; R4/R5 configurations validate with this pin, but their MuonH optimizer cannot be built. Local Qwen and TaskTrove validation stops because `flash_attn` is unavailable. CPU caller tests, lint and type checks pass.

An AdamW async [smoke](https://wandb.ai/dogml/marin-async-rl/runs/3zxyg4gw) on 40 H100s at the pinned runtime completes two nonzero optimizer updates, synchronizes each updated policy to the rollout engine and logs rollout-buffer staleness metrics. The coordinator and HF export job finish successfully, with exported shards matching the index and expected file sizes; the export recovers from one scheduler preemption, while W&B marks the run crashed despite successful Iris exits and complete step-two telemetry.

Part of marin-community/MarinSkyRL#809.

topics.title: Experiment: Hero throughput and expert drops at 8K and 16K context
topics.body:
Agent-driven experiment issue: the runs and this record were produced by a Claude agent, supervised by @mcwitt.

## TL;DR

On one GB200 NVL72 rack, restoring the hero's step-180000 checkpoint at a fixed 4.19M tokens per step, 8K context trains at 297.0k tokens/s, 1.6% below 4K, and 16K at 292.5k tokens/s, 3.1% below 4K. The fraction of expert assignments dropped rises from 1.9e-4 at 4K to 8.3e-4 at 8K (4.5×) and 2.9e-3 at 16K (16×). The drops come from the receiving shard's per-chunk capacity; the ragged transport counts all of them as `sender_dropped` (see the correction comment). Each arm has three seeds; the seed-to-seed standard deviation is at most 0.03 MFU points and 4% to 7% of the drop fraction.

## Description

The hero plan in #8435 moves from 4K to 8K sequences at 50% of training (step ~195k) and to 65K at ~95%. These runs measure what the 8K switch costs in throughput and expert-capacity drops before it happens, with 16K as the next point and a 4K control from the same checkpoint.

Setup:

* Source: `main` at f38da1173de79f1eacd5f54bcfb88db6cb0a9f6e with no code changes. Launcher: `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/launch_diagnostics.py`.
* Checkpoint: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-fa4sm100-nomask-step146k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-180000`, the newest permanent hero checkpoint on 2026-09-30. The current hero run id records that it started from step 146k.
* Hardware and parallelism: one rack (16 nodes × 4 GB200), EP64, the hero's ragged all-to-all transport and capacity factor 1.15.
* Every arm keeps 4,194,304 tokens per step (65,536 per GPU), so the learning rate from the hero's heuristic (`MoeHeuristic` in `experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/heuristic.py`, which scales with tokens per step and total tokens) is the same in all arms. `--schedule-steps 390251` is the hero's full schedule length, so the restored step sits at the hero's position in the learning-rate schedule.
* `qk_mult`, the multiplier on the query-key attention scale, follows the #8435 extension rule `1.3 × (0.1 × ln(seq / 4096) + 1)`.
* Each run trains steps 180000 to 180099 with the production watch interval (10) and coordinated GC interval (100). There is no eval and no checkpoint write.
* The trainer seed sets the data shuffle, so seeds 0, 1, and 2 train on different batches.
* Statistics cover steps 180010 to 180099 (90 steps). Each run contributes its median MFU, median tokens/s, and mean drop fraction; the tables report mean ± standard deviation across the three seeds. Starting the window at step 180030 instead moves no run's median MFU by more than 0.03 points.

| Arm | `--seq-len` | `--batch-size` | `--qk-mult` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4K control | 4096 | 1024 | 1.3 |
| 8K | 8192 | 512 | 1.39 |
| 16K | 16384 | 256 | 1.48 |

Command for one run (8K, seed 0):

```bash
python -m experiments.grug.moe_hero_ep.launch_diagnostics \
  --run-id mhep-ctx8k-s0-20260930 --seed 0 \
  --num-steps 180100 --schedule-steps 390251 \
  --batch-size 512 --seq-len 8192 --qk-mult 1.39 --gc-interval 100 \
  --restore-from s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-fa4sm100-nomask-step146k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-180000 \
  --version dev --run
```

## Results

| Arm | tokens/s | vs 4K | step time | MFU | drop fraction | vs 4K |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4K | 301.9k ± 0.2k | | 13.89 s | 28.25 ± 0.02% | 1.86e-4 ± 0.08e-4 | 1× |
| 8K | 297.0k ± 0.2k | −1.6% | 14.12 s | 28.47 ± 0.02% | 8.29e-4 ± 0.39e-4 | 4.5× |
| 16K | 292.5k ± 0.3k | −3.1% | 14.34 s | 29.37 ± 0.03% | 2.94e-3 ± 0.20e-3 | 16× |

The logged `moe/receiver_drop_fraction` is zero in every run because the ragged transport hard-codes it to zero and counts receiver-capacity clipping as `sender_dropped`. Peak HBM was 103.1 GiB per GPU in every run. In every run, including the 4K control, the mean drop fraction over steps 180055 to 180099 was 0.75 to 1.00 times the mean over steps 180010 to 180054, so part of the measured drop fraction may be a transient after restore.

The live hero (11 racks, 4K) measured over steps 183310 to 183710 on 2026-09-30 had a median MFU of 26.47% and a mean drop fraction of 9.1e-5.

Caveats:

* MFU uses the analytic FLOP count, which charges more attention FLOPs per token at longer sequences (full causal attention on every fourth layer, a 2048-token window elsewhere). MFU therefore rises with sequence length while tokens/s falls. Compare arms by tokens/s.
* The one-rack 4K drop fraction is about 2× the 11-rack hero's. We have not tested the cause. The ratios between arms are the quantity to carry to the hero; an 8K hero drop fraction near 4e-4 is an extrapolation from that ratio, not a measurement.
* Each run covers 100 steps after the switch. Routing over thousands of steps at the new length is untested.
* The 8K and 16K arms change `qk_mult` together with sequence length.
* The diagnostic's peak learning rate comes from a one-rack token budget and is 0.69× the hero's. The diagnostic also leaves the attn_gate/router weight decay at 0 (the hero uses 0.02). Loss values are not comparable with the hero's.
* At 8K and 16K, XLA logged at compile time that rematerialization could only reduce its memory estimate to 193 GiB against a 161 GiB limit. The warning does not stop compilation. The runs trained normally with a runtime peak HBM of 103.1 GiB, the same as 4K, so the estimate overstated actual use.

## Links

* W&B runs (project `marin_moe`, group `moe-hero-ep`): 4K [s0](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx4k-s0-20260930), [s1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx4k-s1-20260930), [s2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx4k-s2-20260930); 8K [s0](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx8k-s0-20260930), [s1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx8k-s1-20260930), [s2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx8k-s2-20260930); 16K [s0](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx16k-s0-20260930), [s1](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx16k-s1-20260930), [s2](https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe/runs/mhep-ctx16k-s2-20260930)
* Hero plan: #8435. 262K context-parallel probe on the same hardware: #8754.

## Conclusion

At the planned 4K to 8K switch, expect about 1.6% fewer tokens per second and about 4.5× the 4K drop fraction, still below 0.1% of assignments on one rack. At 16K the costs are 3.1% and 16×.

topics.title: [rl] Track effective verifier revisions in the Atlas
topics.body:
Bind each SkyRL rating to the verifier mode that produced it, including route code, shared adapters, the pinned verifyit package, and Harbor verifier code. Dataset or verifier changes make the corresponding quality and difficulty evidence stale. Cached refreshes check Harbor history even when MarinSkyRL has not changed.

Review execution checks the captured verifyit commit against the selected checkout. Publication requires every recorded runtime attempt to enable verifyit when Atlas expects it, checks the captured commit against the live Atlas pin, and rejects Harbor evidence when the executed verifier tree differs from the current tree. Harbor commits that leave verifier code unchanged remain eligible.

Remove retired trace-count metadata and assign audited task-specific families to ambiguous TaskTrove sources. Future ambiguous families fail refresh until classified.

The campaign replayed 1,722 preserved model attempts across 32 reviewed sources. These measurements remain tied to their recorded verifier identities.

Builds on #9518.

comments.body:
I didn't catch this, but my agent did. 

`publish_review.py:138-141 validates the installed verifyit commit but never checks that the reviewed runtime attempts enabled verifyit.`

```
 The fix is to validate both the verifier mode and its version before publishing:                                                                                                             
                                                                                                                                                                                               
  • If Atlas expects verifyit, require every recorded runtime attempt to have verifyit_enabled=true.                                                                                           
  • Keep the existing check that its captured package commit matches Atlas’s pin.                                                                                                              
  • Reject missing or mixed-mode evidence before any database writes.                                                                                                                          
                                                                                                                                                                                               
  Add a regression where the package commit matches but verifyit_enabled=false; publication must reject it.              
  
  ```
  
  @weaverbot  can you fix this?
~~On it~~ — this session was relaunched; the live status card is below.

🤖 Fixed in [73271ad23e](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/73271ad23ec604bdb7619550c67c2eebe9a74c9f). When Atlas expects verifyit, publication now requires at least one recorded runtime attempt and `verifyit_enabled=true` on every runtime attempt. Missing, disabled, or mixed-mode evidence is rejected before any database write. The existing captured-commit check against the live Atlas pin remains in place.

Regression coverage includes a matching package commit with `verifyit_enabled=false`, plus missing and mixed-mode attempts. The focused provenance suite passed (9 tests); the branch-selected safe suite passed (2,397 passed, 3 skipped, 5 expected failures). Diff-scoped lint and `pyrefly check` passed.

🤖 Holistic review against current `main`: I would not merge #9628 as a whole. [#10075](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10075) made the curation catalog the source of current Atlas grades and removed `publish_review.py`, the manual verifier declarations, and the old difficulty workflow. This branch now conflicts with those removals. The 1,722 replayed attempts remain useful historical evidence. The mode check in [73271ad](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/73271ad23ec604bdb7619550c67c2eebe9a74c9f) is useful only for any remaining legacy manual publications before the applet cutover.

A TaskSpec already has a [typed grader contract](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d8ac9acfd4f1425e8e6caad28fae70b904e5c5bb/lib/taskcompendium/src/taskcompendium/models.py#L541-L632): verifyit mode and parameters, script, session, or no grader. A `verifyit_enabled` tag would duplicate that contract without proving which code ran. For example, the current [SkyRL IFEval converter](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d8ac9acfd4f1425e8e6caad28fae70b904e5c5bb/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/skyrl/ifeval.py#L35) packages a vendored script grader. Task family labels belong in `SourceInfo.family`; the TaskTrove declarations already assign them.

The new path has useful checks: TaskSpec validates grader configuration; control trials bind the task digest and verification identity; built grader environments hash their verifyit files; assessment keys depend on curation artifacts; publication checks sample coverage. One freshness gap remains if current grades are meant to reflect current verifier code. [`publish_catalog`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d8ac9acfd4f1425e8e6caad28fae70b904e5c5bb/experiments/post_training/task_curation/catalog_snapshot.py#L173-L186) carries an earlier assessment forward when the declaration's pipeline reference and dataset revision match. That reference contains the recipe version and dataset pin, but [no effective grader identity](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d8ac9acfd4f1425e8e6caad28fae70b904e5c5bb/experiments/post_training/task_curation/source_metadata.py#L12-L37). A shared verifier change followed by a partial campaign can therefore retain an old grade for an unrun source. The [Atlas loader](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d8ac9acfd4f1425e8e6caad28fae70b904e5c5bb/infra/marina/applets/rl_data_catalog/load.py#L120-L137) checks source ownership and evidence coverage, but not that freshness relationship. In-process verifyit also relies on explicit stage/version bumps rather than a source-tree digest.

I recommend a focused follow-up on the curation catalog: record the executed grader/artifact identity with the assessment, compare it with the current planned identity before carrying the grade forward, and leave mismatched evidence archived without selecting it as current. Test an unchanged dataset and recipe version with changed verifier code and a partial campaign. Keep grader selection in the structured TaskSpec, not a free-form tag.

Operational caveat: Marina reports Atlas applet version 68 as current, last published October 10; #10075 merged October 14. The versions listing does not identify the deployed commit, so confirm the applet cutover before retiring any legacy publishing procedure.
Oh, @weaverbot is suggesting we don't merge

On it — https://loom.oa.dev/s/ogv09g67
[marin-style-nightly-updates](https://loom.oa.dev/s/ogv09g67/artifacts/marin-style-nightly-updates)

- 🟢 `Oct 15 16:19Z` Fixing verifyit mode validation for PR #9628
- 🟠 `Oct 15 16:41Z` **attention** — Holistic review complete: #9628 is superseded by curation; decide whether to close it and port verifier freshness checks. https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9628#issuecomment-6197270471
- 🟠 `Oct 15 17:00Z` **attention** — Recommendation posted: hold PR #9628; confirm Atlas catalog cutover, then close and port verifier freshness to curation. https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9628#issuecomment-6197656067

🤖 Yes. I recommend against merging #9628 into current `main`. [#10075](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10075) merged on October 14 and made the typed curation catalog the source of Atlas grades. It removed `publish_review.py`, the manual verifier declarations, and the old difficulty workflow that this branch changes. The verifyit mode fix in [73271ad](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/73271ad23ec604bdb7619550c67c2eebe9a74c9f) is valid for legacy manual publication, but merging this branch would revive paths superseded by #10075. The 1,722 replayed attempts remain historical evidence tied to their recorded verifiers.

A freshness gap remains in the new catalog: [`publish_catalog`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/d8ac9acfd4f1425e8e6caad28fae70b904e5c5bb/experiments/post_training/task_curation/catalog_snapshot.py#L173-L186) carries an earlier assessment into a partial campaign when the pipeline reference and dataset revision match. That comparison has no effective grader identity, so a shared verifier change can leave an old grade selected. I recommend a focused follow-up that records the executed grader identity and checks it before carrying an assessment forward.

I would hold this merge and close #9628 once the live Atlas applet's catalog cutover is confirmed. If legacy manual publication must continue before then, port the mode check as a narrow temporary fix.

topics.title: Add Skill2Env to RL Data Atlas
topics.body:
Add NVIDIA's [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) to the RL Data Atlas with a reproducible assessment that helps people decide whether to use the tasks. This issue tracks registration, runnable curation, validation, and publication. Training integration and upstream grader repair remain separate work.

Current status (2026-10-15): catalog registration merged in #10120. The inventory entry is `Harbor Hub:skill2env`, pinned to the 7,496-task Harbor Hub release, version 1.0.1 / revision 2, at `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`. It has no conversion pipeline and is not automatically assessed. Live Atlas publication has not been verified.

The earlier implementation in #9632 is superseded. A separate PR will retrieve the pinned release and connect conversion and native grading to the current task-curation interfaces, retaining the source ID. #9881 also proposes PDBThink registration and remains open for its author to reconcile; #10120 handles its Skill2Env catalog-registration portion.

The previous sampled investigation and verifier-defect reproduction remain evidence for follow-up validation. They do not constitute a completed assessment under the current curation workflow. The old proposed rating, difficulty-eligibility rule, runtime choices, and deployment-reconciliation procedure below are historical, not current completion requirements. The official release and grader remain unchanged.

Remaining work:

- [x] Merge the pinned catalog declaration (#10120).
- [ ] Publish the inventory through a curation campaign, load Atlas, and verify the source entry. Any SAMPLE or FULL campaign includes the inventory; this does not require executing Skill2Env.
- [ ] Add a runnable ingestion/conversion pipeline and validate preservation of native grading behavior.
- [ ] Run a bounded SAMPLE campaign under the current workflow, inspect conversion and grading outcomes, and document unresolved defects and assessment limits.
- [ ] Publish and verify the resulting assessment and evidence in Atlas, then close this intake issue.

<details>
<summary>Historical investigation and superseded implementation plan (before #10120)</summary>

The record below is preserved for its evaluation evidence and implementation history. Status statements, integration questions, and checklists in this section refer to the former #9632 approach and are superseded by the current status above.

Add NVIDIA's [Skill2Env](https://github.com/NVlabs/Skill2Env) to the [RL Data Atlas](https://public.applets.marina.oa.dev/a/fb11c931-5861-4878-8bb5-a964d652b45f/) with an assessment that helps people decide whether to use the tasks. This issue tracks dataset intake, validation and publication. Training integration and repairing the dataset's grader are separate work.

The target is the official [Harbor Hub release](https://hub.harborframework.com/datasets/skill2env/skill2env), revision 2, containing 7,496 tasks. Harbor shows the tags `latest` and `v1.0`; the same release's version field is `1.0.1`. These labels refer to the same content. The paper's private S2EBench evaluation set is separate.

Current status: implementation and sampled validation are prepared in PR #9632, now ready for review. The proposed Atlas rating is "Some issues" because one task's grader was shown to reject valid tests. This rating is not yet published. The official release and its grader remain unchanged; the investigation used two temporary copies with modified reference answers.

The intake can finish with a documented "Some issues" rating. Existing Atlas policy permits the standard Small/Large/Hosted model difficulty comparison only for sources rated "Good", so no difficulty comparison was launched. That is an eligibility decision, not an estimate that these tasks are easy or hard. The three-task quality sample does not establish quality across the full dataset.

Evaluation scope: reported rewards come from the released executable graders. The release also includes written rubrics; the paper's additional LLM rubric-scoring layer was not run or validated here ([§§3.2.2 and 4.2](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.reinforcing-agents-collective-skills.pdf)). Atlas's GLM-5.3 quality audit separately reviews tasks and graders and does not contribute to those rewards.

The PR contains the implementation and concise design rationale. The evidence and integration review questions below support the assessment. The author has marked the PR ready; Ben's Atlas integration review is still pending. The proposed sequence is review, merge, publish, then verify the live entry; this issue stays open through that verification.

### Integration questions for review

- Catalog design: add checked-in Harbor release registrations as an extension to merged #9518. To assess a newer release, a contributor would update the registration through a Marin PR. Atlas refresh would read that registration; it would not automatically switch releases. Evaluation jobs download tasks separately.
- Runtime dependency: retain the review runner's existing MarinSkyRL result adapter and checkout metadata. The catalog entry needs no training registration, but the runner still has this dependency. Review whether to keep it or separate the Harbor runner from MarinSkyRL before landing.
- Agent setup: use Atlas's Terminus-2 with checksum-pinned tools installed offline, preserving the tasks' network restrictions and resource limits. The paper used Pi; these measurements evaluate the Atlas setup.
- Evaluation budget: the sample used a 50-turn limit inherited from Atlas's example configuration. Two of three attempts reached that limit before signaling completion. Review whether this budget is sufficient for initial intake or whether a larger-budget follow-up is needed.
- Scores: preserve all native reward components from the released executable graders, report their arithmetic mean, and count a full pass only when every component reaches one within numerical tolerance. The paper's additional LLM rubric reward was not run. Atlas's separate LLM quality audit does not contribute to these scores.
- Shared tooling: keep the review-output validation, provenance, evidence-retention and provider-call fixes here, or split them into prerequisite PRs.
- Assessment scope: accept the seeded three-task sample as initial intake evidence. It does not establish quality or difficulty across all 7,496 tasks.

Done when:

- [x] Identify the official release and record its task count, source links and license scope in the proposed registration.
- [x] Run the sampled quality review and preserve the original solver, grader and review evidence.
- [x] Assess eligibility for the standard difficulty comparison; currently ineligible under the "Good"-only rule.
- [ ] Review and merge #9632.
- [ ] Reconcile the currently deployed Atlas source with Ben and agree on who will publish the update.
- [ ] Publish and verify the source entry, dated assessment and grading-problem record in Atlas, then close this intake issue.

<details>
<summary>Evaluation results, diagnostic reproduction and evidence identifiers</summary>

The official dataset accompanies [Reinforcing Agents with Collective Skills](https://www.alphaxiv.org/abs/2609.reinforcing-agents-collective-skills). The registered release digest is `sha256:bef4f739bde8d865af04c04a2cb1c84ecad83b52dd558f4d582dd46c7933666c`. Project-owned code is Apache-2.0; third-party task assets retain their own terms.

Sampled evaluation:

Three tasks were selected with seed 42 from all 7,496 pinned release tasks. Every reference-solution reward component was 1 and every no-op component was 0. Task checksums match across those controls and the original GLM-5.3 attempts. All three model attempts reached the native grader without an execution exception; none achieved a full pass.

| Sampled task | Mean component reward | Agent outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ai-seo | 0.93 | Declared completion |
| api-design-reviewer | 0.00 | Used all 50 turns; did not declare completion |
| property-based-testing | 0.25 | Used all 50 turns; did not declare completion |

Scores describe performance within a 50-turn budget. We have not tested whether additional turns improve the two unfinished attempts.

The solver used Terminus-2, GLM-5.3 on Together, Low reasoning effort, and 65,536-total/16,384-output token limits. The Atlas quality-review panel uses GLM-5.3 for three judgments per task and task/source syntheses. All 555 trace-section reviews and 16 original records pass content, schema, reference and evidence-hash checks. The 246 original native artifact files remain byte-identical.

Grader diagnostic:

The task `task_property-based-testing_2kbxlnww` asks the agent to write property tests for a software-version comparison API. A separate diagnostic checked whether its grader wrongly penalizes valid self-comparison tests. Harbor's "oracle agent" runs the supplied reference solution; it is not another model.

The task was pinned at digest `c193f032e03538d875efd6a54026a39621329c2bd88614dab0160b256ed8b4a7`, using official Harbor runner commit `bf991e490394ef9c3250a6db2bc5cbda903cb4c3`. These identifiers make the diagnostic reproducible.

| Reference answer used | Mean native reward | Reference tests | Native mutation result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Authors' original answer | 1.00 | 11 pass | 12/12 killed |
| Same answer with direct self-comparison tests | 0.25 | 12 pass | Skipped by static gate |
| Same tests expressed through a variable alias | 1.00 | 12 pass | 12/12 killed |

To reproduce in a temporary copy, append this property to the reference `solution/test_properties.py`, then run the unchanged native grader through Harbor's oracle agent:

```python
@CI_SETTINGS
@example(Version(1, 2, 3))
@given(valid_versions)
def test_version_reflexivity(version):
    assert version == version
    assert version <= version
    assert version >= version
```

For the equivalent passing control, assign `same_version = version` inside the function and use `same_version` as each comparison's left operand. The grader's `is_self_comparison` compares operand syntax trees; its `no_self_comparison` gate blocks mutation testing for the direct form. The documented task contract does not prohibit valid reflexivity properties on overloaded comparisons.

Only `solution/test_properties.py` in the two temporary diagnostic copies changed. The official release, the grader and the original evaluation artifacts are preserved. All three diagnostic trials completed without an execution exception. They do not replace the original GLM score or establish whether its answer would pass the mutation threshold.

This grading defect supports the prepared "Some issues" assessment. A separate review-panel allegation of leaked SEO helpers was false: the saved trajectory shows the solver creating those helpers. The supplemental review retains the original opinions and replaces their source-level conclusion with the confirmed grading finding. Editable API verifier imports remain a separate concern without a demonstrated exploit.

Evidence and corrections:

Diagnostic job: `/exedev/skill2env-reflexivity-diagnostic-20261002-145621`. Verified diagnostic archive SHA-256: `356b88a8d0c7da1258fbdd669f63d2592991530509571539d90cadc40535a8bb`. Supplemental review SHA-256: `d27b01d25fd27933a1d25a085e65d89b4209afe778f32261a133f3e83c4de79e`.

Independent code review found two problems in the Atlas contribution: omitted trajectory files during publication, and failure to retire the final Harbor registration. Both were fixed in 8df5a15087. These fixes change Atlas tooling, not the Skill2Env grader. A publisher check now retains all nine referenced Harbor summarization files that were missing.

Eight epoch review dates were repaired using native completion timestamps and matching provider-response creation timestamps. The 573 epoch evidence-retrieval references now record their October 2 hash reverification; their original retrieval times are unknown. Original grades, judge opinions and source artifacts remain preserved. No model or native solver runs were repeated for these metadata corrections.

Corrected primary collection SHA-256: `25028bccfca5c246390665e73d8f5cc22a4c6b84a7ea85f4e15169483f7b2da1`. Original collection SHA-256: `e1c4b0befca4292ac8b0afff16a83c29c08278bf627cf81d769e25002b4545e6`. The corrected collection includes the original collection and correction manifests. Supplemental evidence distinguishes the full 7,496-task release from the runner's three staged tasks.

Publication:
